panels.description: Lazy cell loads by the layer that answered them, cheapest at the bottom. The layers are disjoint, so the stack height is the total load rate and its shape is where the reads are being served. state_window, decoded_cache and record_cache are OBSERVED (a record_cache hit skips the store read but still decodes the record). The three store-read layers are INFERRED from how long the read took, cut at 50us and 400us — the geometric midpoints between tiers measured on this deployment's disk (26.3us pebble block cache, 90.3us OS page cache, 1.585ms device). Cross-check them against ${metric_namespace}_storage_cell_db_cache_requests_total{result="miss"}, which is pebble's own accounting and needs no inference: if disk climbs while that stays flat, the thresholds have drifted from this hardware and want re-measuring.
panels.title: Lazy cell loads by layer
